Saginaw band (Ojibwe)

Saginaw is a historical band-name reading route connected to the Saginaw Chippewa Indian Tribe. The 1855 treaty identifies Saginaw parties to the 1837 treaty alongside Swan Creek and Black River parties remaining in Michigan. Read its land-selection terms with community histories and later implementation records.

Read the sources [2] Clarke Historical Library, Central Michigan University; historical treaty text [1] Ziibiwing Center

The Tribe explicitly identifies Saginaw among its three constituent Ojibway bands and explains the Ziibiwing Center. Reuse the cleared exterior only as shared Saginaw Chippewa heritage-center context. It is not a band-specific object, historic village, separate government, boundary or proof of descent. Exterior of the Saginaw Chippewa Tribe’s Ziibiwing Center, a named cultural-history institution. This is the individually named Tribe’s cultural center, not an interior exhibit or every citizen’s portrait. Treaty with the Chippewa of Saginaw, etc., August 2, 1855 — selected transcription ↗

Publication: Treaty dated August 2, 1855; web transcription undated

The 1855 text names its parties and sets out land-selection and payment provisions. It distinguishes Saginaw treaty parties from Swan Creek and Black River parties remaining in Michigan. Historical provisions are not current eligibility, boundaries or proof of fulfillment.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual Saginaw Chippewa and other Bands section, preamble and Articles 1–7, web lines 745–776 read. Other treaties on this long page, original signatures/scans, later implementation and current law not assessed.

Review recorded: October 27, 2026
